newsitem.title: UK: Fast progress with British wheat harvest.
newsitem.headline: Fast progress with British wheat harvest.

text.p: British cereals farmers made fast progress with wheat harvesting over the weekend despite showers in some places, analysts said.
Combine harvesters were working in the counties of the Midlands and East Anglia.
"Big strides have been made over the weekend," an expert at the agricultural consultancy ADAS told Reuters.
By last Thursday, some 25 percent of the crop was in, he said, and around half was likely to be done by next week.
Reported yields varied, but a consensus appeared to be emerging at around half a tonne less than last year, he said.
The 1996 yield was 8.12 tonnes per hectare. According to the Home Grown Cereals Authority, the total UK wheat area rose to 2.026 million hectares in 1997, from 1.976 million a year ago.
